boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Chaffin's Farm/New Market Heights record (September 29-30, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Peebles' Farm (VA074, September 30-October 2) is the co-operating movement south of the James; the October 7 action (VA077) is separate. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Armies' and the live field zero. Humphreys says Ord took 2,000 men from each of two divisions and Birney's column was about 10,000 strong, against Field's three brigades, Fulton's brigade, the local defence and heavy artillery, with ten brigades concentrated at Fort Gilmer for the 30th; he relays Bratton's 1,165 men and 129 officers. Stannard says his division's September 28 field return gave 3,115 for duty, less 260 left in camp.
claims.rationale: Columns, a division field return and one Confederate brigade figure, of different dates; the frozen 'Armies' is not a count. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Humphreys says Fort Harrison was captured with sixteen guns but the attacks on Fort Gilmer failed, and the September 30 assaults were repulsed with heavy loss; Stannard says his division carried and held the position against superior numbers and took 22 guns in all.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Humphreys' sixteen guns in the fort and Stannard's 22 in all the works are different scopes.

Humphreys gives the Adjutant General's table of 394 killed, 1,554 wounded and 324 missing (2,272) for both days, the Medical and Surgical History's Confederate 2,000 and Bratton's 377; Stannard reports 92 killed and 502 wounded in his division on the 29th, with 330 reported missing that he expected to shrink.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Butler's and Ord's reports (Ord No. 314 not read), Birney's, Heckman's and Paine's reports, the colored troops' New Market Heights reports, Ewell's one-line dispatch and Gregg's letter (Nos. 369, 366; read, not selected) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
